briefing.summary: Correction bounce in progress (SPY +0.77%) but with critical bifurcation: cyclicals/value leading (travel +4-5%, gold miners +2-3%, refiners +3%) while mega-cap tech lags (NVDA -1.76%, TSLA -4.79%, AMZN -1.12%). This rotation pattern suggests the market is repositioning away from the names that drove the selloff, not that the selloff is over. FOMC at 2pm EST is the dominant catalyst — rate hold is priced in, the real signal is the dot plot and Powell's press conference tone on tariff-driven inflation. A dovish outcome (2+ cuts maintained, no inflation panic) would likely accelerate the bounce into a short-term rally, especially for rate-sensitive sectors. A hawkish surprise would resume the correction, likely testing the March 13 low of ~5,522. Pre-FOMC conviction should be capped at 50% position sizes — the real edge is in post-announcement reaction trades. VIX at 19.9 is elevated but declining (UVXY -5.93%), indicating fear is peaking rather than accelerating.

recommendations.thesis: Gold broke $3,000 for the first time and the structural bid (central bank buying, ETF inflows, dollar weakness) has room to run. NEM +2.77% yesterday confirms participation but hasn't yet caught up to the gold move — miners typically lag then sprint. FOMC holding rates steady with dovish dot plot (2 cuts maintained) would weaken the dollar further, directly boosting gold. NEM trades at a discount to NAV and has the most liquid options among gold miners. Post-FOMC, if dot plot shows 2+ cuts, gold miners should gap up. Even a neutral FOMC maintains the current gold trend.
recommendations.catalyst: Gold at all-time highs ($3,036), dovish FOMC dot plot would accelerate gold miners. NEM is largest pure-play gold miner with highest operating leverage to gold price.

recommendations.thesis: Cruise lines are showing the strongest group momentum in the entire 181-stock universe (CCL +4.87%, NCLH +4.43%, RCL +3.49%). RCL is the quality play in the group — best balance sheet, highest margins, premium brand. The correction pulled RCL from $270+ to sub-$220, a 19% drawdown that overshot fundamentals for a company with record bookings and pricing power. Ukraine ceasefire reduces European travel risk premium. Oil at $67 is a direct cost tailwind. Post-FOMC, if rates hold and dot plot stays dovish, consumer confidence stabilizes and travel spending sentiment improves. RCL preferred over CCL (too leveraged, bankruptcy history) and NCLH (weakest brand).
recommendations.catalyst: Correction bounce in travel/leisure. Ceasefire + falling oil = tailwinds for cruise operators. FOMC rate hold removes near-term tightening risk for consumer discretionary.

recommendations.thesis: When miners outperform the underlying metal, it signals the market expects the gold move to continue (miners have operating leverage). GDX provides diversified exposure without single-stock risk. The gold thesis is multi-layered: central bank buying (structural), tariff uncertainty (cyclical), rate cut expectations (monetary), and geopolitical hedging (tactical). All four tailwinds are active simultaneously, which is rare. FOMC is the near-term catalyst — even a neutral hold maintains the trajectory. GDX also benefits from improving margins as gold rises faster than mining costs.
recommendations.catalyst: Gold miners ETF — diversified exposure to gold breakout above $3,000. FOMC dovish outcome would be accelerant. Miners outperforming metal (+2.13% vs GLD +0.54%) is bullish breadth signal.

recommendations.thesis: MPC +3.55% is leading the refiner group (VLO +2.95%, PSX +1.94%). The tariff narrative works FOR refiners: they process domestic crude and sell refined products at tariff-inflated prices. Crack spreads (refining margin) have been widening. MPC has the best refining asset base and highest complexity (can process cheap heavy crude into premium products). This is a non-obvious beneficiary of the tariff regime that most traders are overlooking while focused on steel names (which are actually selling off). FOMC is secondary for this trade — refiner margins driven by crack spreads, not rates.
recommendations.catalyst: Refiner margins expanding. 25% steel/aluminum tariffs protect domestic refining infrastructure. Crude at $67 (low input cost) while refined product demand stable. Tariff regime is a structural tailwind for domestic refiners.
